newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP says to spend US$40 mln at San Manuel.
newsitem.headline: BHP says to spend US$40 mln at San Manuel.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Monday it expects to spend about US$40 million on maintenance work in 1998 at its San Manuel copper smelter in the United States.
BHP also said it is studying lifting capacity at the 350,000 tonne a year smelter.
BHP chief executive, copper, Jim Lewis, said any increase in the short-term would be incremental and based on the scheduled maintenance work.
Longer term, the company was in the preliminary stages of looking at more significant increases to capacity, Lewis said.
"It would certainly be possible but all the technology is not there yet," Lewis said.
Additional raw concentrates to support a rise in output from the smelter could come from BHP's Escondida mine in Chile which is earmarked for several stages of capacity increase.

Lewis also told a briefing that recent rainfalls that have enabled copper shipments to resume at BHP's majority Ok Tedi copper-gold mine in Papua New Guinea are not enough to bring operations there back into full swing.
Low water levels following a dry spell stopped river barges from delivering copper concentrate from the mine to the coast for shipment to Europe and Asia at the start of the month.

Weekends rains have enabled some barge traffic to resume, with at least one vessel carrying about 25,000 tonnes of copper concentrate along the Fly River from the Port of Kiunga to the Gulf of Papua for loading.
"The rain so far is not enough in its own right," Lewis said. "If we get three more days of rain we might change our view."
However, he said forecasts strongly suggested that the drought had not yet broken despite the modest rainfall.
